It was past midnight, Zainab's phone was at eleven percent, and the message on it made her hands shake. Sumit: If you really end this, I don't know what I'll do to myself.
They had broken up that evening, calmly, she had thought. Now the old pull was back: go over, say sorry, take it all back.
She plugged the phone into the kitchen socket and stood beside it. She did not take anything back. She typed: "I care about you and I'm taking this seriously. I'm calling someone to be with you right now."
Then she called Sumit's brother Anand, who lived ten minutes away, and read him the message. Anand left at once. While she waited, she called a helpline and followed their advice.
At one, Anand called back: he was with Sumit, and Sumit was safe.
Zainab sat on the kitchen floor and cried. Then she messaged her best friend, who was at her door by two.

qa.a: Sumit got someone who could stay close and help find support, instead of a reunion under pressure that would not have been a free choice.

"If you don't meet me tonight, those chats go to your whole office group," the message from Swati said.
Kamal read it on the crowded metro platform, and for a second the noise went far away. They had ended things a month ago. Since then Swati had tried tears, then silence, then this.
He didn't reply straight away. He took screenshots of this message and the earlier ones. Then he called his friend Yusuf. "I'm not meeting her because of a threat," he said. "But I'm scared."
"Come over," Yusuf said. "We'll report it on the cybercrime site together."
That night, at Yusuf's flat, Kamal wrote to Swati once: "I wish you well, and I'm sorry you're hurting. I won't meet under threats. I've saved these messages." Then he filed the report, blocked her number, and told his team lead briefly, in case anything arrived.
Yusuf made chai. Kamal's hands finally stopped shaking.

qa.a: He read it on the crowded metro platform.

qa.q: How did Kamal feel after reading the message?
qa.a: He was scared; the noise went far away for a moment, and his hands shook until he was safe at Yusuf's flat.

qa.a: He saved screenshots before replying and called Yusuf, which kept the evidence and gave him support instead of reacting alone under pressure.

qa.a: She would see clearly that threats will not work, while still hearing that he wishes her well and is sorry she is hurting.

"Lavanya, what's wrong? You've been staring at your phone for ten minutes," Rehana said, putting down the tea.
"It's Vivek. He says if I don't meet him tonight, he'll send those photos from last year to my office."
Rehana sat down beside her. "Okay. First: you're not meeting him."
"But he said he'll do it. He's so angry. I still care about him, a bit."
"You can care about him and still not give in to a threat. Meeting him alone tonight isn't safe."
Lavanya nodded slowly. "What do I do?"
"Don't delete anything. Take screenshots. Then we call the women's helpline together, now, and tomorrow we go to the cyber cell."
Lavanya typed one line to Vivek: "I won't be meeting you." Then she put the phone face down.
Rehana was already dialling the helpline on speaker. "I'm right here."

passage:
I'm Jomon, and the night before my father's surgery in Kochi, Dolma said something I'll never forget.
"If you go to Kerala, I'll hurt myself. I mean it."
We'd been together three years. I loved her. My hands started shaking. Part of me wanted to cancel the flight just to make the fear stop.
But I knew two things. My father needed me. And a threat like that was too serious to handle alone, or to bargain with.
I said, "Dolma, I love you, and I'm scared for you. I'm not going to leave you alone tonight. And I'm still going tomorrow."
Then I called her sister, who lived twenty minutes away, and a helpline, sitting right beside Dolma on the sofa. The helpline counsellor spoke with her for a long time. Her sister came and stayed.
I took the morning flight. Dolma started seeing a counsellor that month. We're still working things out, carefully.

qa.q: Who came to stay with Dolma that night?
qa.a: Her sister came and stayed.

qa.q: What was Jomon feeling when Dolma made the threat?
qa.a: Jomon felt frightened and torn, loving Dolma but also needing to be with a father facing surgery, with shaking hands.

qa.q: What did Jomon do that was both caring and firm?
qa.a: Jomon stayed with Dolma that night, called her sister and a helpline beside her, and still took the morning flight to his father.

qa.q: How might Dolma have felt when Jomon called her sister and the helpline?
qa.a: Dolma may have felt scared and exposed, but also cared for, since she was not left alone and later began counselling.

grounding: An adult recalls refusing to give in to a partner's self-harm threat while staying kind and getting her immediate support from family and a helpline.

Counsellor's note, family support centre, Tuesday.
Saurabh came in today, steady but tired. His old college friend Chinmay has asked him three times for large loans. Last week, when Saurabh said no, Chinmay said he would tell Saurabh's in-laws about "all his mistakes" from college unless he paid.
Saurabh said, "I still care about him. He's in a bad place. But I'm not going to be threatened into this."
What struck me was how he handled it. He didn't shout back. He told Chinmay calmly, "I won't lend money under threat. If you need help finding work, I'll help with that." Then, the same evening, he told his wife everything himself, before anyone else could.
He's here because he wants support in holding that line and staying kind. We've agreed he will save any further messages, and we've talked about when to involve the police if the threats continue.

qa.q: Who did Saurabh tell everything to the same evening?
qa.a: He told his wife everything himself.

qa.q: How does Saurabh feel toward Chinmay?
qa.a: Saurabh still cares about Chinmay and feels sorry he is in a bad place, but is tired and determined not to be threatened.

qa.q: What did Saurabh do that refused the threat and got support?
qa.a: He calmly refused to lend under threat, offered other help, told his wife himself, and came to a counsellor for support.

qa.q: How might Chinmay feel after Saurabh's calm refusal?
qa.a: Chinmay may feel angry or desperate, since his threat didn't work, while Saurabh's offer of help finding work is still open.

grounding: A counsellor notes an adult who refused a friend's threat of exposure while staying kind, and involved his wife and professional support.

Friday, 11:30 pm
Writing this now because my hands have only just stopped shaking.
At dinner I told Jomon I'm taking the Kochi job and moving out next month. He went very still, then said, "If you leave, I don't know what I'll do to myself."
Two years ago I'd have said, fine, I'll stay. Tonight I said, "I care about you a lot. I'm still taking the job. And I'm taking what you just said seriously." I didn't leave him alone. I sat with him on the sofa and called his sister Mercy; she came over within the hour. While we waited I rang a helpline, and they talked me through what to say and what to watch for. Mercy is staying the night, and she'll take him to see a doctor tomorrow.
I'm not guilty for having my own life. I'm also not walking away from him.
Thomas
